chapter: Recording dates, Goodman and band life
title: Studio scheduling in New York: Jim and Andy's and how Milt Hinton stayed fit
summary: Jones explains the three-hour session pattern and how drinking between sessions could ruin an evening date.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. So, well, we started at 9:00 o'clock, see, because usually in New York -- I don't know how it is now -- dates would go like 10:00 to -- three hours unless it goes overtime -- 10:00 to 1:00, then 2:00 to 5:00, and then there's a dinner break. You know, everybody --

And then it starts from 7:00 to 10:00 at night. Now, you have to watch that 7:00 to 10:00 at night, because they go to Jim and Andy's and go to the bar. You have to catch them early in the morning, get them early in the day.
To get the mileage out of them, you know?

Because I remember there was one time when I think it was Grady Tate and Ernie Roth, had an early morning date, then there was a whole lot of time in between, until 7:00 o'clock at night, and they got into Jim and Andy's and started eating and getting logey and drinking and partying, till they had to send somebody in their place, because they couldn't cut that date in that shape.
And there was no way for them to do it, you know? See, you have to be -- it's dangerous, you know. You got to know how to do that, especially in Manhattan.
Like Milt and some of the more experienced guys, Milt Hinton, they would always eat.
Eat. And Milt's wife, Mona, would keep some -- he was eating vitamin pills like peanuts, you know?

To keep his energy up, keep him in good shape, you know? And so consequently they never got in any trouble. They would have their drinks and have their fun, but they never got into any trouble by being run down or anything, you know?
